contract: story 224 (a long synthetic campaign across repeated restarts) against DAYS = 7 at tls.py:58

remediation: `_spent` asks openssl `x509 -checkend` before either is reused; a spent root is reissued and takes its leaves with it, keeping the signing key so the pin survives

contract: proxy.py log_error: every served and every refused request has a row behind it; Refused is the module's own name for a request that will not be forwarded
evidence: `Fence._bind` executed the bind with no guard at all twelve call sites, each of which wrapped only the query that followed, so a session left in an aborted transaction raised `pg.DatabaseError` past handlers that catch `Refused` and the exchange got no Receipt, no answer and no log line
remediation: the bind is guarded once inside `_bind` and raises `Refused("program bind refused")`, so the caller answers 502 and the record that can still be written is written

contract: proxy.py log_error: every served and every refused request has a row behind it, and the one thing that leaves no row is said out loud
evidence: `pg.ConnectionError_` (src/redkraken/pg.py:98) is a sibling of `pg.DatabaseError` and not a subclass, so a session that went away escaped every typed guard in the door, reached socketserver, and dropped the socket with no answer, no row and nothing telling the caller whether the door or the target had stopped
remediation: `_serve` wraps the decision, answers 502 under its own `door-unavailable` token and logs the line `log_error` exists for; `_release` and the blocked-receipt write name both classes so a bookkeeping failure still answers
